question.problem:
Let $\mathcal{B}=\{\mathbf{b}_1,\mathbf{b}_2,\mathbf{b}_3\}$ be a basis of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and let $\mathcal{S}$ be the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}^3.$ Find the values of $a,b,$ and $c$ if 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275083/assets/957c59d27a871a52f110c3dca91cec390091c13ceba6e14d6485f92aa150c51a.svg)

and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{S}$ is 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275083/assets/6095f1a65a9b9b245de2dd4cad611d2616a2b3b15e4701fe33c3c53b913c2283.svg)
question.worked_solution:
Recall  that the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}^3$ consists of the vectors $\mathbf e_1, \mathbf e_2,$ and $\mathbf e_3,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275083/assets/41bd0d4956d8ec09d0339a79329c6739e07e698d9dee9f192968d77c9ec28842.svg)

The components of the vectors in $\mathcal{B}$ are just the coordinates relative to the standard basis:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275083/assets/30a1bdc2316f5d7acc527cb1d69fc11c7b732f9e22a4d57a11ed84f2db1e3cd5.svg)

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{S}$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{S}.$ 

Therefore, we obtain
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275083/assets/5606e00ccc39829e3c599aa86286dcc1f1cb4e3febb280adf4e1bbe18dc7ab6a.svg)

Finally, $a=0,$ $b=0,$ and $c=10.$
